subject: Day trips GetYourGuide sells from London
scope: Research only. No article written, nothing in src/ touched. This file is an inventory for a future day-trips page, and a check on what GetYourGuide actually has before any widget is embedded.

method.enumeration: widget.getyourguide.com/default/activities.frame with partner_id=WWP7I0R, locale_code=en-GB, currency=GBP, number_of_items=20 and a browser User-Agent - the same frame the site's data-gyg-q embeds hit. 207 distinct search queries across two sweeps (46 for the named destinations, 96 for destinations not named, plus a location_id pass), one request at a time with a 0.8s pause. 1,175 distinct products seen.
method.parsing: The frame's sibling activities.json endpoint 404s, so the records come out of the astro-island props attribute in the frame HTML. Every value there is serialised as [tag, payload]; unwrapping it recursively yields tourId, title, price.startingPrice, price.currency, duration, stars, reviewCount, categoryLabel, abstract, primaryLocation and urlToAdp. Script: scratchpad gyg-lib.mjs (not committed - it was a throwaway).
method.verification: Every candidate id was fetched back one at a time as activities.frame?number_of_items=1&tour_ids=<id>. A live, bookable id echoes back with a fresh price, rating and review count. A dead, delisted or unbookable id returns a valid but EMPTY frame - the frame never 404s, so emptiness is the reject signal. 698 ids checked, 695 live, 3 rejected.
method.productPages: Inclusions, exclusions and departure points were read off the product page for 23 products. The canonical slug URL 302s; https://www.getyourguide.com/en-gb/activity/-t<id> returns 200. curl gets 403 from Cloudflare after one or two pages, so these were read in the browser. Every other product in this file is widget-frame data only and its record says so.
method.gapChecks: Destinations the keyword sweep returned nothing for were checked against the live site through DuckDuckGo, because GetYourGuide's own /s/?q= search ignores the q parameter and returns geo-default inventory. That found Thorpe Park, the Lake District, Brussels, Cardiff, Bletchley Park and Warwick Castle products the widget search had missed.

nonDeterminismWarning: Confirmed again here. The same query, same parameters, minutes apart, returns a different set: 'Bletchley Park from London', 'Brussels day trip from London', 'Lake District from London' and 'Thorpe Park from London' all returned twenty unrelated London products rather than nothing, because the frame silently falls back to generic London inventory when it has no match. A data-gyg-q slot for any of these destinations would render Stonehenge coaches. Use data-gyg-tour-ids with the verified ids in this file for anything load-bearing.

demandSignalsWorthAPage.note: Product count is a supply signal, and supply on GetYourGuide tracks what converts. These are the destinations with enough inventory to carry their own page, in order.
readAcrossTheTop: Stonehenge (60 products) is not really one destination - almost every product pairs it with Bath, Windsor or Oxford. A Stonehenge page is in practice a 'which Stonehenge combination' page.
The Cotswolds (47) is the strongest standalone case: the villages have no useful railway, so the coach tour is the only realistic way in and nothing is competing with a train fare.
Bath (36) and Windsor (36) are both heavily cannibalised by the Stonehenge combinations - only 2 of 36 Bath products are Bath alone.
Oxford (31) and Cambridge (9) are wildly asymmetric given they are the same kind of trip and similar distances, which is itself an angle.
Dover/White Cliffs (18) and Canterbury (16) are the same coach trip sold twice; treat Kent as one page.
Thorpe Park and Chessington have ZERO London-departure products - only gate tickets (ids 111550 and 112474, both GBP 32). So does Cardiff, where both former day trips are now dead ids.

otherThingsToAvoid: Warwick Castle has no standalone London product at all - all 7 are four- and five-stop coach marathons (Oxford + Stratford + Cotswolds + Warwick in 10 hours). Never describe one of those as a Warwick Castle day trip.
Bletchley Park has exactly one London-departure product, id 1322959 at GBP 995 with zero reviews, and Bletchley is 40 minutes from Euston with the park next to the station. Do not embed it.

The Lake District has exactly one live product, id 2273 at GBP 349 (Euston, return train, cruise, cream tea, 4.4 on 64 reviews). The other id the search engines still index, 16139, returns an empty frame - it is dead.
Brussels has exactly one, id 932751 at GBP 329 with zero reviews. Nothing in this file justifies recommending it over booking Eurostar direct.

Cardiff: both products are dead (67689, 16142). GetYourGuide does not currently sell a Cardiff day trip from London. Wales means North Wales via 630344 at GBP 259 - which does include Caernarfon Castle entry and reserved train seats, on only 7 reviews.

Edinburgh at GBP 219 (16135) and York at GBP 149 (883112) are rail packages wrapped round a hop-on hop-off bus. Edinburgh is 4h20 each way from King's Cross; a day trip is nearly nine hours on trains.

Zero-review products are everywhere in the long tail - 1408799, 1408818, 1408831, 1408855, 1409283, 1409685, 1409894, 1411758, 1441567, 1446148, 1453215, 1456664, 1460124 and more are all new listings at 0/0 priced above the established equivalents. Several are clearly the same itinerary relisted. Never surface one.

Several destination names collide badly in search: 'Leeds Castle' products sometimes render as 'London: Leeds, Canterbury...' which reads like the city of Leeds, and 'Stratford' matches Stratford in east London. Filter on the full name.

Price drift: the frame returned EUR rather than GBP on a handful of calls mid-sweep (1345509, 1460124, 1183194, 440187, 553881, 173934 among them) with no parameter change. Re-read any price in this file before publishing it, and never hard-code a currency symbol next to a widget.

findings: GetYourGuide sells day trips from London to 35 destinations with at least one live product; two more (Thorpe Park, Chessington) exist only as gate tickets with no London departure, and Cardiff's two products are now dead ids.

224 live London-departure products across those destinations, of which 219 are single-day trips and 5 are multi-day escorted tours. A further 5 London-departure products matched no destination bucket.
Four destinations carry over 30 products each: Stonehenge (60), the Cotswolds (47), Bath (36) and Windsor (36). Oxford is close behind at 31.

The conditional-inclusion pattern is the single biggest hazard on the platform, and it is the main thing this research turned up. Of 23 product pages opened, 10 name an attraction in the title and then make its entry an 'if option selected' extra: 945 ('IF PURCHASED'), 52393, 166535, 156657, 50354, 70842, 2257, 106654, 391446 and 60796. Between them they hold roughly 22,000 reviews, and several lead the widget ranking. 70842 is the worst drafted - the Stonehenge ticket appears in its includes list AND its excludes list.

Where entry IS genuinely included the titles say so and the pages back it up without a conditional clause: 219849, 16096, 61147, 71088, 1116311, 64192, 1128430, 70032, 645578, 2271, 16135 and 630344 were all checked on the page. That list, not the title, is what a recommendation should rest on - 'with Entry Ticket' in a title proves nothing, because 156657 and 50354 say much the same and mean the opposite.

Most day trips leave from a handful of points, not Victoria: Gloucester Road Underground (61147, 60796), Urban Baristas by South Kensington station (215430, 395005), the Lycee Francais on Cromwell Road (219849), Blackfriars (106654), Greenline Coach Station behind Victoria station but explicitly not Victoria Coach Station (799068), Tooley Street by London Bridge (1128430), Vauxhall Bridge Road by Victoria (70032), and Euston for every rail package (2273, 2271, 630344, and the Studio Tour train product).

Rail packages are a distinct and thinly reviewed category: Euston for the Lake District (2273), Liverpool (2271) and North Wales (630344); King's Cross for Edinburgh (16135) and York (883112); St Pancras for Paris (11098) and Brussels (932751). None has more than a few hundred reviews and several are under ten.

Only three destinations in this inventory are realistically NOT doable by train instead: the Cotswolds villages, the Jurassic Coast around Durdle Door, and Glastonbury/Cheddar. Everywhere else the honest answer is that a train works, and often works better - which is the angle a day-trips page on this site should take.
